slides.heading: Longest Increasing Subsequence
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Longest Increasing Subsequence, a very hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: One strictly increasing subsequence of maximum length (patience sorting with predecessor links).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. One strictly increasing subsequence of maximum length (patience sorting with predecessor links).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Patience sorting: keep the smallest possible tail for each length and binary search where each number goes.
slides.narration: Patience sorting: keep the smallest possible tail for each length and binary search where each number goes.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: DP: for each i check all j < i → O(n²)
Patience sorting tails + binary search → O(n log n)
slides.narration: The classic DP is quadratic. Keeping the smallest possible tail for each length, and binary-searching where each value goes, is n log n.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, tails array of indices. Second, binary search the position. Third, record predecessors. Fourth, rebuild from the last tail.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 5 → tails[0]
slides.narration: Binary search where 5 fits among the tails: position 0. It extends the longest so far.

slides.heading: Worked example

slides.narration: Binary search where -24 fits among the tails: position 0. It replaces a larger tail, keeping that length's tail as small as possible.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each i, binary search tails for the first value not less than a i, set prev to the index before, store i, and grow length if at the end. Then follow prev from the last tail.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: tails isn't the LIS itself — rebuild with prev
slides.narration: The tails array isn't the sequence; keep prev pointers to rebuild it.

bullets: Patience sorting: keep the smallest possible tail for each length and binary search where each number goes.
